solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It points right on golf course

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing written on another comes straight after it

blocks.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a course is a route taken
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A signpost on a golf course showing players which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a direction sign; 'points' is the bricklayer's verb, filling the joints between tiles or bricks with mortar or grout.
explanation.definitionFit: To point brickwork is to fill its joints, so a worker who applies grout to tiles does that job.

clue.text: Good old Ford model right for small racer

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
O is the standard abbreviation for old
the Ka is a small Ford car
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Praise for a vintage Ford car that is well suited to small-scale racing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ka was a small Ford hatchback sold mainly in Europe; RT is a less common abbreviation than R for right.
explanation.definitionFit: A kart is a tiny low open vehicle raced on short tracks, so it counts as a miniature racing machine.

clue.text: Not seeing lake, I will cut through plain

indicators.note: something that cuts through another ends up lying inside it

blocks.note: plain as in clear, evident
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot see a lake vows to cut across the flat countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like a noun for flat land, but it is the adjective meaning clear; the lake and I split it after OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unaware of what is around you means failing to notice things, which the clue phrases as not seeing.

clue.text: Paint (not on paper) like an artist?

blocks.note: tempera is a paint made with egg yolk
something done only in the head is not written down

explanation.surface: Painting directly rather than sketching first, the way a true artist works.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like a painting tip, but it describes doing something in your head rather than on paper. The question mark flags the stereotype of the moody artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists are proverbially moody and volatile, so behaving like one means acting in an unpredictable, emotional way.

clue.text: Fell, removing top of skin

indicators.note: taking off the top drops the first letter of a down answer

blocks.note: to skin your knee is to graze it

explanation.surface: Someone took a tumble and scraped the top layer off their skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as the past tense of fall, but it is the verb meaning to cut or knock down; 'skin' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a building or tree is to bring it to the ground, exactly what razing does.

clue.text: Take a mouthful from Cheers VIP, say?

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak the words, matching sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: cheers is a casual British goodbye, and a toff is an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A celebrity guest at the Cheers bar is offered a nibble of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' suggests the TV bar or a toast, but in Britain it also means goodbye; a toff is a posh, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: To bite off a piece of food is to take one bite into your mouth, as in biting off more than you can chew.

clue.text: Working party, caught by surprise, waste time

indicators.note: what is caught by something is held inside its grasp

blocks.note: to boggle is to amaze, as in mind-boggling
a machine that is working is on
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A committee is surprised by events and squanders its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working party' reads as a committee but splits into two pieces; boggle is used here as a verb meaning to astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: Boondoggle is American slang for pointless busywork, and as a verb it means to fritter away hours on trivial tasks.

clue.text: Time to pay for quite a few?

definitions.text: Time to pay for quite a few?

blocks.clueFragment: Time to pay for quite a few?
blocks.note: surface reading: a moment when you settle the bill for a large order
setter's reading: quite a few drinks, paid for with a hangover the next day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay for' sounds like settling a bill, but it is suffering the consequences; 'quite a few' is the drinker's euphemism for a lot of alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: The hungover period after a night of heavy drinking is when the body makes you suffer for your excesses.

clue.text: Hunter, or one almost catching one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
to catch something is to hold it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then trimmed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hunter, or someone who very nearly catches their quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'one's do different jobs: the first is cut to ON and joined to OR, and that pair catches the second, the Roman numeral I, in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is the great hunter of Greek mythology, also the constellation named after him.

clue.text: One aim — blocking hunt that’s cruel

indicators.note: a block placed in a passage sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: to fish for something is to hunt for it
I is the Roman numeral for one
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: An activist's single goal is stopping a cruel fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests protest against blood sports; 'hunt' is a verb meaning to search, as in fishing for compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiendish person behaves like a devil, delighting in inflicting pain, which is synonymous with being cruel.

clue.text: Priest protected by Hummer in US city

indicators.note: what is protected is surrounded and shielded on all sides

blocks.note: a kazoo is played by humming into it
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A cleric is driven around an American city in a Hummer, the big military-style SUV.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes 'Hummer' look like the vehicle; it is anything that hums, here a kazoo.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamazoo is a city in southwestern Michigan, famous partly for its comical-sounding name.

clue.text: Refugee from former French island

blocks.note: an ex- is something former
île is French for island

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing a former French colony in the islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on île is dropped in the grid, as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person forced to live away from their homeland, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: 14 struggle with criticism

blocks.note: the answer to 14, the Royal Engineers, are abbreviated RE
to vie is to compete or strive
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Army engineers battling against harsh feedback.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 14-across, a British army corps whose standard abbreviation is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic's written assessment of a book, play or film is a piece of criticism published in print.

clue.text: Met radio presenter with no idea about hugging

indicators.note: turned about suggests letters spun round into a new order
to hug is to wrap your arms around, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
a DJ, or disc jockey, presents a music radio show

explanation.surface: Meeting a clueless radio host who goes round hugging everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like London's police or the Metropolitan Opera, but it is the past tense of meet, in the sense of touching at a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin share a border, so adjoined is a formal past tense for touched or came together.

clue.text: Rights abandoned, scrutiny provokes revolutions

indicators.note: what is abandoned is left behind, so those letters disappear

blocks.note: a search is a close scrutiny
to provoke someone is to anger them
two rights, R and R, are the letters to remove

explanation.surface: With civil liberties gone, official snooping stirs people to rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Rights' means two Rs, one dropped from each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea change is a profound transformation, a phrase from The Tempest, so plural sea changes are radical upheavals.

clue.text: Senior general wrong to capture unknown soldiers

indicators.note: a wrong arrangement is not the proper order, so the letters are reset
a captive is held inside its captor's grip

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x and z

explanation.surface: A top commander is mistaken to take anonymous troops prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters must also take in the unknown, so Y joins the fodder before the final order appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Engineers are the British Army corps of military engineers, so its members are soldiers.

clue.text: Wonder what a lid could be?

blocks.note: first meaning: a surprising revelation
second meaning, whimsical: an eyelid is what uncovers the eye

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' suggests a pot or jar, but here it is an eyelid; the question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing that changes how you see things is a revelation, and the eyelid literally uncovers the eyeball.

clue.text: Before trial, butters up the best-dressed

indicators.note: going up a down answer means reading from bottom to top
what comes before is placed in front of the next piece

blocks.note: rams butt with their heads, so they are butters
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Flatterers sucking up to fashionable people ahead of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butters up' reads as flatters, but 'butters' is a noun, animals that butt, and 'up' is a separate instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smart means looking neat and elegantly clothed, so the superlative describes whoever is most stylishly turned out.

clue.text: New style car parts guard braking component

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters take a fresh order
to part something is to split it open so a piece can sit in the gap

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A newly styled car has a protective guard over its brake parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car parts' looks like a single phrase about spares, but 'parts' is a verb, the rearranged letters splitting the guard.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hydraulic brake system the master cylinder converts pedal pressure into fluid pressure, a key element of the brakes.

clue.text: Wry and artfully witty about a bit of sex

indicators.note: done artfully means cleverly reworked, so the letters are rearranged
a bit of a word is a single small piece, its opening letter
to be about something is to surround it

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sly, clever joke touching on something a little risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wry and artfully witty' reads as one description, but only 'Wry' defines; 'artfully' works on the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry originally means bent or turned aside, as in a wry neck, so it shares the sense of twisted or contorted.

clue.text: Hand in substantial payment

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: something substantial is real, having physical existence
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: Submitting a large sum of money as payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand in' looks like a phrasal verb meaning submit, which suits remittal nicely, but 'Hand' and 'in' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit money is to send it to settle a debt, so a remittal is the sum transmitted as settlement.

clue.text: Think about old touchpad alternative

indicators.note: to be about something is to go around it on every side

blocks.note: to muse is to think or ponder
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Considering what to use instead of an outdated laptop touchpad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'about' instructs the first word's synonym to go round 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a laptop you can steer the pointer either with the built-in pad or with a separate handheld pointing device.

clue.text: Fruit seen in hands

blocks.note: paw is informal for a hand
the plural asks for a second one

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted holding a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paw' is jokey slang for a human hand, and the plural is spelt out as two of them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawpaw is another name for the papaya, a tropical orange-fleshed fruit, and also a North American tree fruit.

clue.text: Go quiet, making little noise

blocks.note: to go is a polite euphemism for urinating
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Falling silent and barely making a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go quiet' reads as one phrase meaning hush; 'Go' is the bathroom euphemism, and P is musical shorthand for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a faint chirping sound, as in not hearing a peep out of someone, so it is a small sound.

clue.text: Part of one qualifying match

indicators.note: a part of a phrase is a stretch of its letters, read straight through

blocks.note: letters read across the word boundary

explanation.surface: One leg of a qualifying fixture in a football tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like the game in the surface but is the verb meaning to be the same as.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to be its equal in size, quality or ability, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A Scot’s tears are his

blocks.note: first meaning: in Scots, to greet is to weep
second meaning: the plural of hi, a salutation

explanation.walkthrough: 'his' looks like the possessive pronoun but is the plural of the salutation hi. Greet meaning cry is a Scottish dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Each hi is a salutation, so several are salutations; in Scots dialect, greeting is weeping, so a Scot's tears count as well.

clue.text: Makes patterns — all square, of course

blocks.note: a game that is all square is level
of course is an emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: A golfer who is level with an opponent, playing on a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' hints at a golf course, which suits 'all square', golf's phrase for a level match, but it simply means certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie-dye fabric is to knot it before dyeing so that swirling designs appear, creating decoration on cloth.

clue.text: Left before light show

indicators.note: what comes before is placed in front of the next piece

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone departed before the laser light show began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed, and 'light show' as one event; port is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict or represent it, so show works as a verb meaning represent.
